name: GoodRx Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: GoodRx operates the leading U.S. digital platform for comparing prescription drug prices and accessing negotiated discount codes usable at pharmacies nationwide, monetized primarily through fees from pharmacy benefit managers. It also runs Pharma Direct (manufacturer-sponsored savings and affordability programs), the GoodRx Gold subscription, and telehealth services. Under CEO Wendy Barnes (since January 2025), the mix is shifting toward Pharma Direct, which grew 76% YoY in Q2 2026 while the legacy prescription-transaction business declined. Market cap is roughly $1.2B at $3.55 per share.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): GoodRx has built a significant new revenue stream in Pharma Direct, manufacturer-funded affordability programs that grew 82% YoY in Q1 2026 and 76% to $61.6M in Q2 2026, alongside subscription revenue up 39% to $28.5M [1][2][4]. AI Deployment (1/2): The company has shipped AI-assisted consumer features such as scan-and-search drug lookup and runs internal AI hackathons and use-case pods, but has not quantified AI-driven savings or revenue [5]. Market Share (2/2): GoodRx is the category-defining consumer prescription-savings brand, and its Pharma Direct channel reportedly captured about one-third of early Wegovy pill cash-pay sales [10]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management is expanding the Integrated Savings Program and manufacturer partnerships and raised 2026 guidance twice, but no named next-gen products have dated launch milestones [1][2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D was $121M in FY2025, about 15% of revenue, which is high for a healthcare-information platform [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): GoodRx's stated purpose is to help Americans get the healthcare they need at a price they can afford. The statement is specific and tied directly to the product, which lowers out-of-pocket drug costs, and employees cite it as a rallying point [7]. Community Impact (0/2): The searches found no distinct foundation or quantified charitable program beyond the core consumer-savings product. A 2019 report that regulators said GoodRx shared users' health data with advertisers also undercuts its consumer-trust record [9]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and leadership has turned over repeatedly: the co-CEOs stepped down, an interim CEO followed, and Wendy Barnes took over in January 2025 [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying by executives was identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth stock. D/E is 83.2% (0.94) and TTM ROE is just 2.6% (0.17, 2x weight) [3]. TTM revenue fell about 1.8% YoY to $785M (0.61), while the FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR is 7.7% ($551M to $797M; 0.85, 2x) [3]. Forward P/E is about 11.7x, derived from the $3.55 price and the FY2026 consensus adjusted EPS of $0.30 (1.0). TTM GAAP net margin is 2.1% (0.10). The provider's forward PEG of -4.26 is negative and scores 0 (2x) [3]. Weighted sum 4.69/10 gives a score of 5. The liquidity floor is passed: 1.29M shares x $3.55 = about $4.6M traded per day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): GoodRx's moat is its contracted PBM pricing network and brand-driven consumer traffic, not proprietary physical assets. AI assistants and search answers that surface drug prices directly could cut the consumer traffic that drives its prescription-transaction revenue, which already declined in 2026 [1][2]. The faster-growing Pharma Direct business depends on manufacturer relationships and point-of-sale integration, which AI is less likely to replace, and that partly offsets the exposure [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): GoodRx uses AI internally and in features such as scan-and-search, but it reports no quantifiable AI revenue [5].

infinite_game.summary: GoodRx's affordability mission is service-oriented and real, and the move toward manufacturer-funded Pharma Direct shows some adaptability. However, repeated CEO turnover, a data-privacy controversy, and dependence on PBM economics read more as a company managing a shrinking legacy business than one shaped by a durable Just Cause. Sinek would see a worthy purpose that leadership has not yet shown it can hold through instability.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The goal of making prescriptions affordable for every American is idealistic, service-oriented, and visible in the product, and employees describe rallying around it [7]. It has not yet held through a stable leadership era, so it is a genuine cause that is only partly lived rather than a proven competitive advantage [6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management has shifted investment toward Pharma Direct and subscriptions while the legacy prescription-transaction business shrinks, accepting flat consolidated revenue to build the new engine [1][2]. GAAP profitability, however, remains thin, at a 2.1% net margin [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Leadership has been disruptive, with the co-CEOs stepping down, an interim CEO, and a new CEO in 2025, followed by a reshuffle of the COO and product roles [6]. Employees report trust internally, but no retention data offsets the instability [7].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The pivot from a pure consumer coupon platform to manufacturer affordability programs and subscriptions is a real business-model evolution, with Pharma Direct expected to grow more than 70% in 2026 [2]. It is still adjacent to the core savings business rather than a reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): The searches found no management commentary framing rivals such as SingleCare, Cost Plus Drugs, or Amazon Pharmacy as sources of learning. Competitive discussion centers on defending share and pharmacy economics [2].

investment_thesis: GoodRx is moving from a PBM-dependent coupon business toward manufacturer-funded Pharma Direct and subscriptions. Pharma Direct revenue rose 76% to $61.6M and subscriptions rose 39% to $28.5M in Q2 2026, and management raised FY2026 guidance to $790-805M revenue and $240-250M adjusted EBITDA [1][2]. At $3.55 the stock trades at about 8x EV/EBITDA, roughly 12x FY2026 consensus adjusted EPS of $0.30, and a 12% free-cash-flow yield [3]. Debt is modest at 83% of equity, and buybacks have cut the share count from about 412M in 2022 to about 339M [3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that the core prescription-transaction business keeps shrinking. Total revenue fell 1.3% YoY in Q2 2026 despite Pharma Direct's growth, and TTM GAAP net margin is only 2.1% with ROE of 2.6% [1][3]. Retail pharmacy closures, PBM contract renegotiations, and AI search tools that surface drug prices directly all threaten the traffic engine. Repeated CEO turnover and a past health-data privacy controversy raise governance and execution risk [6][9]. The Inspire score of -49 (MISALIGNED, abortion activism) is a significant concern for faith-based mandates.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results in early November: a return to YoY revenue growth, which management signaled could come earlier than planned [2]
Pharma Direct reaching more than 70% growth for FY2026 as GLP-1 and other branded cash-pay programs scale [2][10]
Continued share buybacks funded by about $146M of TTM free cash flow, a 12% FCF yield [3]
key_risks: Continued decline of the legacy prescription-transaction business as pharmacy closures and PBM economics shift [1]
AI assistants and search answers surfacing drug prices directly and cutting consumer traffic [5]
Leadership instability and privacy or regulatory scrutiny over the use of consumer health data [6][9]
